tiles.title: The Braided Lava Confluence
tiles.family: Lava tube: anastomosing distributaries and collapsed western feeder
tiles.description: Braided lava distributaries join around a remnant central core and four lateral pockets. A genuine two-lane western roof-fall obstruction forces travel through the confluence or around the eastern conduit. Exact five-foot modular mouths are maintained for five feet inward. Roof heights, rock stability, and lava history are conjectural.

zones.interpretation: A localized drooped upper feeder roof restricts upright travel; the deeper confluence and lower distributary remain viable.

tiles.title: The Sagging Sheetflow
tiles.family: Inflated basalt sheet-flow cave: deflated blisters, remnant septa and a raised lava bench
tiles.description: A contrasting low sheet-flow cave with six asymmetric interconnected vesicles and a doglegged southern transfer around surviving basalt ribs, a drained central basin, and a surviving elevated basalt bench approached by three transitions. A double-width northwest ceiling fall interrupts an axial route, forcing a verified detour without disconnecting the eight five-foot modular mouths. All roof clearances and formation stages remain hypothetical.

tiles.title: The Split-Spine Drainback
tiles.family: Lava tube: drained channel bifurcation around a persistent basalt septum
tiles.description: A drained volcanic conduit divides around a five-cell-deep preserved central basalt spine. A narrow inflated roof blister links the upstream branches while the lower confluence drains toward a recessed pressure chamber. The west limb is severed by three distinct fallen-roof edges, obliging a long circuit through the eastern limb. The plan, not a cave survey, establishes floor topology; roof thickness, headroom, gradients and structural stability are not measured.
